title: A predictive, causal map of the genome’s regulatory code

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a quantitatively reliable account of how changes to DNA alter gene regulation in specified cellular conditions. Given a DNA sequence, a proposed modification and a cellular context, it would predict which genes are affected, how their RNA production or processing changes, and the size of those effects. Its scope includes noncoding regulatory sequences and distant regulatory elements whose effects depend on the cells and conditions in which they operate.

Conceptual synthesis: The causal part of this map would come from prospective agreement between predictions and controlled interventions at native genomic locations. A model that reproduces observed RNA patterns or ranks associated variants provides useful predictive evidence, but that alone does not establish what changing a particular sequence will cause. Even successful intervention predictions would establish a causal capability for specified outcomes and contexts; they would not necessarily reveal every molecular step connecting the sequence change to the outcome.

significance.text: Within a validated domain, this capability would let researchers predict many regulatory effects before constructing the corresponding variants. It could guide which variants to test, connect regulatory elements to their target genes and make experiments more informative. Genetics would gain a stronger ability to formulate and test quantitative mechanistic hypotheses alongside association studies. The Borzoi paper explicitly connects the predictive goal to interpreting potentially pathogenic mutations and prioritizing functional variants at loci identified by genome-wide association studies.

Conditional impact synthesis: Reliable regulatory predictions could improve disease-variant interpretation and help researchers design therapeutic changes to gene activity. Those possibilities depend on additional knowledge: how regulatory changes affect cells, tissues and whole-organism physiology; whether an intervention reaches the relevant cells; and whether its benefits outweigh unwanted effects. Predicting an RNA outcome would not by itself establish disease causation, clinical efficacy or a complete explanation of the underlying mechanism. The advance would therefore be foundational for experimental genetics without making association studies or physiological experiments unnecessary.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is dependable quantitative prediction of the effects of previously untested regulatory perturbations across a clearly specified range of genomic and cellular contexts. The supplied Borzoi evidence illustrates concrete obstacles: most tissue-specific splicing events were not captured well, and target-gene prioritization in one supplementary evaluation was close to a distance-based baseline. These findings expose gaps in learning context specificity and assigning regulatory effects to the correct genes. They support limitations in that model, rather than a definitive judgment about every subsequent model.

Engineering synthesis: A broader causal map would need to resolve how distant elements influence genes, distinguish regulatory layers such as RNA production and splicing, and predict effect magnitudes rather than merely rank variants. It would also need to handle combinations of changes and structural alterations, including cases in which the effect of one change depends on another. Generalization across tissues, developmental stages, genetic backgrounds and environments would require explicit evidence rather than an assumption that a relationship learned in one context transfers to another.

Validation synthesis: Establishing this capability requires experimental data that separate causal effects from correlated sequence features and observations. Predictions must be tested against perturbations at native loci, with controls that make the measured outcome interpretable. The model must also express uncertainty and recognize inputs outside its demonstrated competence. The supplied record does not establish whether the full capability remained open throughout the field as of 1 November 2026; it establishes a substantial objective and specific limitations in the documented Borzoi work.

current_state.text: Linder, Srivastava, Yuan, Agarwal and Kelley published Predicting RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence as a unifying model of gene regulation online on 8 January 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41588-024-02053-6. The supplied review identifies matching bibliographic information and substantive main-text and supplementary material. The paper reports Borzoi, a model that predicts cell-type-specific and tissue-specific RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence, together with regulatory variant-effect benchmarks. These are documented advances in predicting regulatory readouts and evaluating variants, not a demonstration of a causal map for arbitrary genomes and conditions.

Borzoi was also evaluated on linking distant regulatory elements to genes using experiments that inhibited regulatory elements with CRISPR interference and measured gene expression. This supplies a perturbation-based test of regulatory prediction, but inhibition of an element is a different intervention from making a specified DNA substitution or structural change. The reported difficulties with tissue-specific splicing, target-gene assignment and quantitative variant effects further limit what can be inferred from its benchmark performance.

The Borzoi evidence is available only with inspection limits in the supplied review. The main HTML and main-paper PDF text extractions were truncated, and the PDF extraction reported that some form content was skipped. The identified supplementary text used for the target-gene limitation was untruncated, but figure images were not inspected. These limits constrain detailed interpretation without negating the bibliographic identity or the findings supported by the reviewed passages.

The earlier research attributes Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome to Avsec and colleagues, gives a publication date of 28 January 2026 and DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10014-0, and describes improvements on multiple regulatory benchmarks. Those details remain attributed claims from the supplied research: the corresponding artifact available to the review contained only a cookie challenge, with no abstract or paper text. The review therefore could not verify the publication details or benchmark results from document content. This access failure is not evidence that the paper or its reported results are false.

Evidence-scope synthesis: No bounded freshness-search record was supplied. Consequently, these materials support a dated account of Borzoi and an unresolved report concerning AlphaGenome, rather than a comprehensive assessment of the field through 1 November 2026. They neither demonstrate completion of the proposed innovation nor justify an exhaustive claim that every current approach lacks it.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Define in advance the genomes, tissues, developmental stages, genetic backgrounds, environmental conditions and regulatory outcomes covered. Within that domain, predict the quantitative effects of thousands of previously untested substitutions, structural changes and combinations. Include distant regulatory elements and cases selected independently of the model developers. The numerical scale and breadth are proposed evaluation choices, not established scientific completion standards.
completion_criteria.label: Quantitative predictions cover thousands of untested changes within predefined domains

completion_criteria.text: Proposed experimental validation: Independent teams would introduce the specified changes at native loci and measure the prespecified outcomes, including relevant RNA abundance or processing endpoints. Suitable controls would distinguish effects of the intended sequence alteration from experimental artifacts. Evaluation should distinguish direct sequence editing from other useful perturbations: the CRISPR-interference experiments described in the Borzoi study ground the rationale for testing distant regulation, but do not themselves satisfy this proposed sequence-editing demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Independent native-locus sequence editing validates predicted RNA regulatory effects

completion_criteria.text: Proposed acceptance and reproducibility criteria: Preregister accuracy requirements, acceptable quantitative errors, uncertainty-calibration thresholds, baselines and rules for handling inconclusive measurements. Test generalization to independently selected contexts and assess whether the model flags cases beyond its competence. Independent replication should reproduce the main predictive findings with enough methodological detail to compare outcomes. Passing would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested domain; finite experiments could not establish literal universality across all sequences, organisms or conditions.
completion_criteria.label: Predictive findings meet preregistered criteria and replicate independently

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: GEN-02, Design and construct complex eukaryotic genomes to specification, could use GEN-01 predictions to choose regulatory sequences that produce desired behavior. Genome construction additionally requires reliable assembly and biological functioning at much larger scales. GEN-03, Precise, programmable replacement of large genomic regions in existing cells, concerns the ability to install changes; it could enable demanding tests of GEN-01, whose central task is predicting their regulatory consequences. GEN-04, A retargetable delivery platform for genetic medicines across the body, concerns reaching the appropriate cells. Accurate regulatory predictions would help choose an intervention, while delivery would remain a separate requirement.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-05, General laws of environmentally induced, sequence-independent inheritance, overlaps with GEN-01 through environmental context and inherited regulatory states. Its central question is persistence of effects without a DNA-sequence change, whereas GEN-01 centers on predicting regulatory consequences of sequence perturbations in specified contexts. GEN-11, Predicting genetic interactions across backgrounds and environments, overlaps directly with predicting combinations of regulatory variants and context-dependent effects. GEN-11 has a broader focus on interactions among genetic changes and their outcomes; GEN-01 specifically targets the mapping from sequence changes to regulation.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-06, Transferable clonal seed reproduction across major crops, concerns achieving a particular reproductive capability. GEN-07, Predictably controllable inheritance in wild populations, concerns how inheritance behaves and can be controlled at population scale. A regulatory map might inform interventions relevant to either objective, but predicting gene regulation would not demonstrate clonal reproduction or controlled inheritance in populations. GEN-08, Reconstructing an organism’s cell divisions and histories from inherited molecular marks, concerns recovering lineage history. Such histories could help characterize developmental contexts for GEN-01, but lineage reconstruction and prediction of regulatory perturbations are distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-09, An autonomous, evolvable expanded genetic alphabet, concerns a biological system that maintains and uses additional genetic letters. GEN-10, A testable reconstruction of the origin and fixation of the genetic code, concerns the historical emergence of the coding system. Neither is equivalent to GEN-01's regulatory code: here, code refers to relationships between DNA sequence, cellular context and gene regulation, rather than the nucleotide alphabet or the assignment of codons to amino acids.

unresolved_issues: AlphaGenome's reported authorship, publication date, DOI and benchmark improvements remain unverified from document content in the supplied record.
The empty freshness-search record prevents a comprehensive assessment of progress or remaining openness through 1 November 2026.
Borzoi's main-text extractions are partial, some PDF form content was skipped, and figure images were not inspected; conclusions requiring those materials remain outside the reviewed evidence.
The proposed demonstration still requires concrete choices of covered genomes and contexts, endpoints, accuracy thresholds, calibration requirements and replication procedures.
The anomalous reporting summary's relationship to Borzoi remains unresolved; it was excluded without treating the mismatch as evidence against the correctly identified paper.

brief.title: Predicting how DNA changes affect gene activity
possible: Researchers could predict what a proposed DNA change would do before making it in a cell. They could identify the genes affected, predict how much RNA—the genes’ molecular output—they produce, and anticipate how that RNA is processed under specified conditions.
why: This would help researchers choose more informative experiments and connect stretches of DNA that control gene activity to the genes they influence. It could also help interpret disease-linked DNA changes and guide the design of treatments that alter gene activity.

sources.who: Johannes Linder and colleagues at Calico and Sanofi
sources.showed: Their Borzoi model predicts RNA measurements from DNA across different cells and tissues. It also predicts effects of DNA changes on RNA production and processing.
sources.quote:
Here, we introduce Borzoi, a model that learns to predict cell-type-specific 
and tissue-specific RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence.
sources.cited_for: Borzoi demonstrates that DNA sequence can support predictions across several layers of gene activity.
sources.not_established: Its performance does not establish reliable quantitative predictions for previously untested DNA edits across cellular conditions.

sources.who: Žiga Avsec and colleagues at Google DeepMind
sources.showed: Their AlphaGenome model predicts several kinds of gene activity from DNA, resolving individual DNA letters. It matched or exceeded leading models on most tests of DNA-change effects.
sources.quote: predicts thousands of functional genomic tracks up to single-base-pair resolution across diverse modalities.
sources.cited_for: AlphaGenome demonstrates broader prediction of molecular effects from DNA sequence.
sources.not_established: Benchmark success does not establish prospective agreement with independent experiments making specified DNA edits in their natural locations.

shown: Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome combines long stretches of DNA with detailed predictions across several kinds of gene activity. Linder and colleagues’ Borzoi also links distant control regions to genes in tests that suppress those regions. Suppression tests differ from testing a specified DNA edit.
missing: Dependable predictions must give the size of effects on the correct genes, including effects from distant control regions.
Predictions must handle combined changes and larger DNA rearrangements, including changes whose effects depend on one another.
Independent experiments must confirm predicted RNA effects of previously untested edits across clearly defined cells and conditions.

milestones.label: Quantitative predictions cover thousands of untested DNA changes
milestones.explanation: Predictions would have to cover thousands of untested substitutions, rearrangements and combinations, including distant control regions, within a predefined scope. This would establish the breadth claimed before experiments begin.

milestones.label: Independent DNA edits confirm predicted RNA effects
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to make the specified edits at their natural DNA locations and measure RNA production or processing with suitable controls. This would test whether the edits cause the predicted effects.

milestones.label: Predictions meet agreed standards and replicate independently
milestones.explanation: Results would have to meet preregistered accuracy and uncertainty standards, generalize to independently chosen conditions and replicate independently. This would establish reliability within the tested scope.

uncertain: The required accuracy, acceptable errors and range of cells and conditions still need concrete definitions.
Predicting an RNA change does not by itself explain every molecular step or establish disease causation or treatment benefit.

page.title: Quantitative prediction of regulatory variant effects
page.definition: A genome-wide model predicts which human genes a single-nucleotide substitution—a replacement of one DNA letter—affects, and the direction and size of changes in RNA abundance and processing in specified cellular conditions. Controlled edits at native chromosomal locations validate these predictions.

goal.need: IGVF describes a prediction space containing billions of possible single-nucleotide variants, about 20,000 genes and thousands of cell types. Measuring every combination is infeasible. Its programme therefore combines experimental perturbations with models that predict effects for untested variants and cellular contexts.

completion.title: Independent native-locus editing validates quantitative regulatory predictions across withheld cellular contexts.
completion.criterion: A genome-wide model passes prospective tests in human cellular contexts excluded from model development. For previously unmeasured single-nucleotide edits at native loci, including distant regulatory DNA, it predicts target genes and the direction and magnitude of RNA-abundance and splice-usage changes. Predictions agree with measurements within independently estimated assay uncertainty, and another laboratory reproduces the result. The covered contexts, endpoints and uncertainty model are fixed before testing.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body’s end-to-end acceptance criterion was found for this capability.
completion.basis: Searches of NHGRI/IGVF programme targets, CAGI assessment rules and the de Boer–Taipale roadmap found no native-edit accuracy and replication threshold spanning cellular contexts. The roadmap proposes withholding genomic sequences from training, but supplies no numerical accuracy cutoff. This provisional test confines achievement to experimentally verified quantitative effects within a declared domain.

milestones.title: Reporter assays detect regulatory variant effects at P ≤ 10−5.
milestones.criterion: Under the CAGI5 plasmid-reporter protocol, an expression effect has confidence score ≥0.1, corresponding to P ≤10−5. The 2018 dataset covered approximately 17,500 single-nucleotide variants in five enhancers and nine promoters, with three experimental replicates. AlphaGenome, published on 28 January 2026, reported Pearson r=0.65 for its supervised CAGI5 effect-size benchmark.
milestones.set_by: Critical Assessment of Genome Interpretation, CAGI5 Regulation Saturation experimental protocol and assessment rules.
milestones.threshold_quote: A ‘significant expression effect’ in the provided data is one assigned a confidence score greater than or equal to 0.1.

milestones.title: More than 100,000 candidate regulatory element–gene interactions are measured.
milestones.criterion: Measure more than 100,000 candidate element–gene relationships. Borzoi’s evaluation, published on 8 January 2025, included 10,051 candidate pairs 98–262 kb from transcription start sites in a CRISPR-interference dataset. This benchmark does not establish completion of the aggregate target. CRISPR interference suppresses an element without introducing a specified nucleotide substitution.
milestones.set_by: NHGRI-funded IGVF Consortium, 2024 programme paper, gene-regulation experimental targets.

milestones.title: Expression effects are tested for thousands of noncoding variants.
milestones.criterion: IGVF accepts fine-mapping of expression quantitative trait loci—variant–expression associations—or CRISPR genome editing; it gives no exact minimum beyond “thousands”. Borzoi reported mean Spearman correlation 0.334 between predicted and association-derived effect sizes across 49 GTEx tissues. AlphaGenome reported recovery of 41% of GTEx expression-associated variants at 90% effect-direction accuracy on 28 January 2026.
milestones.set_by: NHGRI-funded IGVF Consortium, 2024 programme paper, gene-regulation experimental targets.

milestones.title: A map supplies regulatory predictions for every possible human single-nucleotide variant.
milestones.criterion: Supply the regulatory component of IGVF’s genome-wide variant map. On 8 September 2026, DeepMind announced AlphaGenome Atlas, containing predictions for nine billion single-nucleotide variants across hundreds of human and mouse cell types and tissues. This developer-announced catalogue result is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: NHGRI-funded IGVF Consortium, Box 2 of its 2024 programme paper; this milestone tracks the regulatory component of its broader map objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: every possible SNV in the human genome

milestones.title: Native-locus edits validate quantitative regulatory predictions in one human cellular context.
milestones.criterion: A frozen model prospectively predicts target genes, RNA-abundance changes and splice-usage changes for previously unmeasured single-nucleotide edits at withheld native loci in one specified human cellular condition, including distant regulatory elements. Editing confirms quantitative agreement within independently estimated assay uncertainty. No externally specified sample size or numerical acceptance cutoff was found. The cited association, reporter and element-inhibition benchmarks do not establish this result.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; searches of NHGRI/IGVF targets, CAGI rules and the cited roadmap found no prospective native-edit acceptance threshold.

not_found: No published end-to-end accuracy and replication threshold was found for quantitative native-edit predictions across human cellular contexts.
No aggregate experimental result establishing IGVF’s target of more than 100,000 candidate regulatory interactions was found.
No prospective native-edit study establishing the completion criterion was found.
